opioid_prescribing_limits.value: Boards must adopt rules establishing penalties for prescribing opioids in dosage amounts exceeding what would be prescribed by a reasonably prudent prescribing practitioner.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: Any board created under this chapter that licenses a prescribing practitioner shall adopt rules under chapter 17A establishing penalties for prescribing practitioners that prescribe opioids in dosage amounts exceeding what would be prescribed by a reasonably prudent prescribing practitioner engaged in the same practice.
opioid_prescribing_limits.citation: [UMBRELLA / Chapter 147 - GENERAL PROVISIONS, HEALTH-RELATED PROFESSIONS] Section 147.162 - Rules and directives relating to opioids.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician assistants may prescribe, dispense, order, administer, or procure prescription drugs, controlled substances, or medical devices necessary to complete a course of therapy pursuant to section 148C.4.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: a physician assistant may prescribe, dispense, order, administer, or procure prescription drugs, controlled substances, or medical devices necessary to complete a course of therapy pursuant to section 148C.4.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: A licensee shall have a continuing duty and obligation, as a condition of licensure, to report to the licensing board by which the licensee is licensed every adverse judgment in a professional or occupational malpractice action to which the licensee is a party, and every settlement of a claim against the licensee alleging malpractice.
malpractice_reporting_required.citation: [UMBRELLA / Chapter 272C - REGULATION OF LICENSED PROFESSIONS AND OCCUPA] Section 272C.9 - Duties of licensees.

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: A full and confidential report concerning any final hospital disciplinary action approved by a hospital board of trustees that results in a limitation, suspension, or revocation of a physician's privilege to practice for reasons relating to the physician's professional competence ... shall be made to the board of medicine by the hospital administrator or chief of medical staff within ten days of such action.
hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.citation: [UMBRELLA / Chapter 147 - GENERAL PROVISIONS, HEALTH-RELATED PROFESSIONS] Section 147.135 - Peer review committees — nonliability — records and reports privileged and confidential.

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: Establish a licensee review committee for the purpose of evaluating and monitoring licensees who are impaired as a result of substance use disorder, dependency, or addiction, or by any mental or physical disorder or disability, and who self-report the impairment to the committee, or who are referred by the board to the committee.
impaired_physician_program_authorized.citation: [UMBRELLA / Chapter 272C - REGULATION OF LICENSED PROFESSIONS AND OCCUPA] Section 272C.3 - Authority of licensing boards.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: The board may, upon probable cause, compel a physician to submit to a mental or physical examination by designated physicians or to submit to alcohol or drug screening within a time specified by the board.

administrative_medicine_license_availabl.quote: An application for an administrative medicine license shall be made to the board.
